description.value: This study investigated the neural mechanisms of hypnosis-based smoking-aversion suggestions using fMRI and EEG, focusing on smoking-cue responses, prefrontal-insula connectivity, and the temporal order of activation.

spans.text: The present study exploits functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and electroencephalograph (EEG) to examine the treatment effects of hypnosis on cigarette smoking and investigate the underlying neural mechanism of hypnosis in reducing smoking craving.

value: Finally, we predict that activation in the prefrontal regions should antecede activation in the insula, suggesting a top-down control process.
We further predict that the insula would be functionally connected to the prefrontal regions during the experience of hypnotic aversion suggestions.

description.value: Two groups of smokers underwent separate fMRI or EEG sessions. The fMRI group performed a smoking-related cue task in control and hypnotic states on independent days, with the control state scanned first; the EEG group performed a similar task during EEG data collection.

spans.text: One group performed a smoking‐related cue task twice during fMRI scanning (in control and hypnotic states, respectively), whereas the other group performed a similar task during EEG data collection.
